If you're asking about
safely deflating a bus tire
for maintenance, repair, or replacement, here are the proper steps:
Safe Tire Deflation Process
Equipment needed:
Safety cones or warning triangles
Tire gauge
Valve stem tool or screwdriver
Safety glasses and gloves
Proper parking location
Steps:
Park safely
- Position the bus on level ground, away from traffic, with parking brake engaged
Locate the valve stem
- Find the air valve on the tire you need to deflate
Deflate gradually
- Use the valve stem tool to slowly release air. Press the tool gently into the valve to let air escape at a controlled rate
Monitor pressure
- Use a tire gauge to check remaining pressure as you deflate
Complete deflation
- Remove all air until the tire is fully flat (if removing the tire)
Document the work
- Record the deflation in your maintenance log for safety and legal compliance
Legal Considerations
Always document
any tire work in official maintenance records
Follow regulations
- Commercial buses must comply with DOT and state regulations for tire maintenance
Inform management
- Report any tire issues to your supervisor/fleet manager
Use proper procedures
- Follow your company's safety protocols
If this is for a fleet operation, consult your maintenance manual or contact a certified technician. Professional tire shops can handle this work if you're uncertain about the process.
